outcome: As of 11 Oct 2026 the exact conjecture is still open for k ≥ 7 (every K7-minor-free graph is 6-colourable) on every source I opened; the in-window movement is (a) a preprint (Norin and Steiner, arXiv:2610.05291, 4 Oct 2026) proving the linear form (χ(G) ≤ C·h(G) for an absolute constant C), whose abstract says the proof 'was found by GPT-6 Astra'; (b) a follow-up (Wood, arXiv:2610.10831, 7 Oct 2026) giving C = 19,885,160; (c) an improvement of the Delcourt–Postle bound to O(t log log log t) (Liu and Luo, arXiv:2609.06867, 6 Sep 2026); (d) restricted-class results; and (e) a Japanese SIG-AM abstract claiming a full proof, which I could not verify.
problem_asks: (1) For every loopless graph G, χ(G) ≤ h(G), where h(G) is the largest t such that K_t is a minor of G: every graph with chromatic number k has a K_k minor, for every k ≥ 1. (2) Equivalently in colouring form: for every t, every graph with no K_t minor is (t−1)-colourable. The statement asks for this exact inequality (chromatic number against clique-minor size). It does not name a linear, asymptotic, dominating, odd, or restricted-class version.

events.what_happened: Hadwiger's 1943 paper introduces the conjecture. Wikipedia says the k=4 case was proved in that paper. A search snippet also attributes k ≤ 3 to Hadwiger and Dirac. I did not reach the 1943 paper itself.
events.delivers: Poses the conjecture. Per Wikipedia, settles k=4 (every K4-minor-free graph is 3-colourable); k ≤ 3 is elementary.
events.remains: Every k ≥ 5.
events.direction: Asserts χ ≤ h for all graphs; the conjecture itself, not a result on it.

events.what_happened: Wagner (1937) showed the k=5 case (every K5-minor-free graph is 4-colourable) is equivalent to the four-colour theorem, as recorded on Wikipedia. The journal of publication was not checked.
events.delivers: Reduces the k=5 case to the four-colour theorem (an equivalence, so the case holds given the four-colour theorem).
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Kostochka and Thomason, independently, showed graphs with no K_t minor have average degree O(t√log t) and so are O(t√log t)-colourable. Wikipedia dates this 1984; the Postle and Norin–Postle–Song abstracts say 1980s.
events.delivers: Order-of-magnitude bound χ = O(t√log t) for K_t-minor-free graphs. Not the exact bound.
events.remains: Exact (t−1) bound for all t; any linear or near-linear bound.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a weaker form.

events.what_happened: Robertson, Seymour and Thomas proved the k=6 case (every K6-minor-free graph is 5-colourable), using the four-colour theorem. Wikipedia says their paper won the 1994 Fulkerson Prize. The journal of publication was not checked.
events.delivers: Settles k=6 (conditionally on the four-colour theorem, which is itself a theorem).
events.remains: k ≥ 7, i.e. every K7-minor-free graph is 6-colourable (the first open case).

checked_by.who: Robertson, Seymour, Thomas (authors); result recognised by the 1994 Fulkerson Prize per Wikipedia
checked_by.qualification: Authors are leading graph minors researchers; the Fulkerson Prize is a refereed-prize recognition of the paper
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the proof; the prize recognises it

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for k=6.

events.what_happened: Kawarabayashi and Toft showed every 7-chromatic graph has a K7 or K4,4 minor, equivalently every graph with no K7 and no K4,4 minor is 6-colourable, as recorded on Wikipedia (dated 2005). The venue was not checked.
events.delivers: Partial result on the K7 case: restricted to graphs with no K4,4 minor as well as no K7 minor.
events.remains: The K7 case without the extra K4,4 exclusion; the full HC(7).
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a restricted-class case of k=7.

events.what_happened: Norin, Postle and Song posted 'Breaking the degeneracy barrier for coloring graphs with no K_t minor' on 21 Oct 2019 (v2 27 May 2020). Every graph with no K_t minor is O(t(log t)^β)-colourable for every β > 1/4, improving O(t√log t).
events.revisions: v1 21 Oct 2019; v2 27 May 2020 (listing says it combines with arXiv:1911.01491).
events.delivers: Order-of-magnitude improvement: χ = O(t(log t)^β) for every β > 1/4. Not exact.
events.remains: Exact (t−1) bound; any linear bound.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a weaker form (bound on χ).

events.what_happened: Postle posted 'Further progress towards Hadwiger's conjecture' (arXiv:2006.11798, v1 21 Jun 2020). It claims O(t(log t)^β)-colourability for every β > 0 and, combined with another paper, O(t(log log t)^18). Version 4 (18 May 2022) is withdrawn; its comments say the content was merged into arXiv:2108.01633.
events.revisions: v1 21 Jun 2020; v2 23 Jun 2020; v3 3 Jul 2020; v4 18 May 2022 withdrawn.
events.delivers: Bound χ = O(t(log t)^β) for every β > 0, and O(t(log log t)^18) combined with another paper. Withdrawn; the content is in arXiv:2108.01633.
events.remains: Exact (t−1) bound; linear bound.

withdrawn.what: Version 4 withdrawn; comments say merged into arXiv:2108.01633

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a weaker form (bound on χ).

events.what_happened: Delcourt and Postle, 'Reducing Linear Hadwiger's Conjecture to Coloring Small Graphs', arXiv:2108.01633, v1 3 Aug 2021. They show every K_t-minor-free graph is O(t log log t)-colourable, reduce the linear conjecture to small graphs, and prove linear colourability for K_t-minor-free graphs with clique number at most √(log t)/(log log t)². The arXiv record lists no journal reference. A Toronto Metropolitan profile says the paper appeared in J. Amer. Math. Soc. in 2025; I did not confirm this from a primary source.
events.delivers: χ = O(t log log t) for K_t-minor-free graphs. Linear colourability for K_t-minor-free graphs with clique number at most √(log t)/(log log t)², hence linear HC for K_r-free graphs for each fixed r. Reduction: the linear conjecture reduces to small graphs. Not exact.
events.remains: Exact (t−1) bound; the linear conjecture for general K_t-minor-free graphs.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a weaker form (bound on χ, and a restricted linear case).

events.what_happened: Tong Li and Qiang Zhou, 'Hadwiger's Conjecture for some graphs with independence number two', arXiv:2305.05868, v1 10 May 2023; v5 30 Mar 2024. They prove the conjecture for H-free graphs with independence number two, for some specified graphs H. The abstract page does not name the H's.
events.revisions: v1 10 May 2023; v2 11 May 2023; v3 18 May 2023; v4 30 Jul 2023; v5 30 Mar 2024 (in window).
events.delivers: The conjecture for H-free graphs with independence number two, for the H's specified in the paper (not named on the abstract page).
events.remains: The conjecture for general graphs with independence number two, and for graphs not H-free.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a restricted-class result.

events.what_happened: Illingworth and Wood, 'Dominating K_t-models', arXiv:2405.14299, posted 23 May 2024. They define dominating K_t-models (every vertex of each later branch set has a neighbour in each earlier one), show graphs with no dominating K4-model are 2-degenerate and 3-colourable, give a 2^(t−2) bound on average degree, and propose a dominating strengthening of Hadwiger's conjecture. It is not a result on the original conjecture.
events.delivers: Dominating variant only: dominating K4-model case (2-degenerate, 3-colourable) and a 2^(t−2) average-degree bound for dominating K_t-models. Does not address the original conjecture.
events.remains: The original conjecture is untouched; the dominating variant is open in general.
events.direction: Does not bear on the original conjecture's truth; it defines a stronger variant. A dominating K_t-model is a K_t minor, so the dominating variant implies the original.

events.what_happened: Rong Chen and Zijian Deng, 'Seymour and Woodall's conjecture holds for graphs with independence number two', arXiv:2406.02643, v1 4 Jun 2024. They prove that for each ℓ with 2ℓ ≤ χ(G), a graph with independence number two has a K^ℓ_{ℓ,χ(G)−ℓ} minor, which establishes the Seymour–Woodall conjecture (every graph has every complete bipartite graph on χ(G) vertices as a minor) for those graphs. The abstract page does not mention Hadwiger's conjecture.
events.delivers: The Seymour–Woodall complete-bipartite-minor conjecture for graphs with independence number two. A different conjecture from Hadwiger's, in the same circle of ideas. Says nothing about K_k minors for all k.
events.remains: The Seymour–Woodall conjecture for general graphs, and the Hadwiger conjecture.
events.direction: Different question: a complete-bipartite minor statement, not the clique-minor statement. Silent on the Hadwiger conjecture on the abstract page.

events.what_happened: Norin and Totschnig, 'Every graph with no K7∨-minor is 6-colorable', arXiv:2507.03244, posted 4 Jul 2025. K7∨ is K7 with two edges sharing an endpoint deleted. The paper proves K7∨-minor-free graphs are 6-colourable. A talk abstract by Totschnig (Waterloo, Feb 2026) reports the same K7∨ statement; I treat it as the same result.
events.delivers: Restricted class: every K7∨-minor-free graph is 6-colourable. K7∨-minor-free graphs are a subclass of the K7-minor-free graphs, so this is a special case of the K7 case of the conjecture, not the case itself.
events.remains: Every K7-minor-free graph (the K7 case of HC).
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a restricted-class case of k=7.

events.what_happened: Costa, Luu, Wood and Yip, 'Verifying Hadwiger's Conjecture for Examples of Graphs with α(G) = 2', arXiv:2512.17114, v1 18 Dec 2025, v2 22 Dec 2025. They prove the conjecture for inflations of the complements of graphs with girth at least 5, triangle-free Kneser graphs, and the Clebsch, Mesner and Gewirtz graphs, all with independence number two. They identify classes where the α=2 case is open. The HTML they publish includes a computer check ('computationally verified Conjecture 10 (CDM) for all graphs up to 11 vertices'); that is computer search, not AI, and I did not establish which conjecture CDM is.
events.delivers: Restricted class: the conjecture for the listed inflations of complements of certain graphs (independence number two). Does not prove the general α=2 case.
events.remains: The general α=2 case, and the conjecture for all other graphs.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; restricted-class results.

ai.note: Computer search only; read to 100,000 of 166,252 characters of the HTML.

events.what_happened: Kühn, Sauermann, Steiner and Wigderson, 'Disproof of the Odd Hadwiger Conjecture', arXiv:2512.20392, posted 23 Dec 2025. They prove there exist graphs with no odd K_t minor and chromatic number at least (3/2 − o(1))t, disproving in a strong form the odd Hadwiger conjecture of Gerards and Seymour (1993). The abstract says nothing about the original conjecture.
events.delivers: Disproves the odd variant: graphs with no odd K_t minor and χ ≥ (3/2 − o(1))t. The odd variant implies the original (an odd minor is a minor), so this does not disprove the original; the abstract is silent on it.
events.remains: The original conjecture is untouched.
events.direction: Cuts against the odd variant, not the original. The odd variant is a stronger statement, so a counterexample to it does not decide the original.
events.object: Existence (the abstract says 'there exist') of graphs with no odd K_t minor and chromatic number at least (3/2 − o(1))t. Method not confirmed from the full text; a secondary summary says it uses a random model of triangle-free graphs, which I did not verify.

ai.note: Abstract and metadata page only; full text not read.

events.what_happened: Carter and Yip, 'Hadwiger's Conjecture for {co-claw, co-gem}-free graphs and {fork, antifork}-free graphs', arXiv:2605.28050, posted 27 May 2026. They prove the conjecture for these two induced-subgraph-free classes, and prove a stronger statement: every {co-claw, co-gem}-free graph has a K_χ-model with branch sets of at most two vertices, and every {fork, antifork}-free graph has one with at most one branch set larger than two.
events.delivers: Restricted class: the conjecture for {co-claw, co-gem}-free graphs and {fork, antifork}-free graphs (with the stronger model statements). Does not cover all graphs.
events.remains: The conjecture for all other graphs.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; restricted-class result.

ai.note: Abstract page only; no AI or computer statement on the page.

events.what_happened: Girão, Norin, Tamitegama and Tan, 'Two Relaxations of the Dominating Hadwiger's Conjecture', arXiv:2608.12126, posted 12 Aug 2026. They prove that graphs of average degree of order t(log t)² contain a dominating K_t-model (improving 2^(t−2)), and that the vertices of a graph with no dominating K_t-model can be partitioned into t−1 parts each inducing bounded maximum degree. This concerns the dominating variant only.
events.delivers: Dominating variant only: average-degree threshold for dominating K_t-models, and a partition relaxation. Since a dominating K_t-model is a K_t minor, the dominating variant implies the original; these results do not settle the original.
events.remains: The dominating conjecture in full, and the original conjecture.
events.direction: Does not bear on the original conjecture's truth; relaxations of a stronger variant.

systems.name: ChatGPT 5.6 Sol
systems.what_it_did: Authors' words: used 'to fill in the details of the proof of Theorem 2 and reorganize parts of it', and separately 'used for proofreading the paper'. Theorem 2 is in the dominating variant, not the original conjecture.
systems.basis_quote: ChatGPT 5.6 Sol and Codex were later used to fill in the details of the proof of Theorem 2 and reorganize parts of it.

systems.name: Codex
systems.what_it_did: Same statement as above: helped fill in the details of the proof of Theorem 2 and reorganise parts of it.
systems.basis_quote: ChatGPT 5.6 Sol and Codex were later used to fill in the details of the proof of Theorem 2 and reorganize parts of it.

events.what_happened: Chun-Hung Liu and Jason Luo, 'Beyond halfway to Hadwiger's conjecture', arXiv:2609.06867, v1 6 Sep 2026; v2 9 Sep 2026 with the comment 'significantly improve the bound and change the title'. They prove every graph with no K_t minor has chromatic number O(t log log log t), improving Delcourt and Postle's O(t log log t).
events.revisions: v1 6 Sep 2026 (its title and abstract were not read); v2 9 Sep 2026 (comment: 'significantly improve the bound and change the title').
events.delivers: χ = O(t log log log t) for K_t-minor-free graphs. Not exact; a bound-moving result on the quantity the conjecture bounds.
events.remains: Exact (t−1) bound; linear bound.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; a weaker form (bound on χ).

ai.note: Abstract and metadata page only; full text not read.

events.what_happened: Dvořák, Norin and Rahman, 'Every graph with no K7^= minor is 6-colorable', arXiv:2609.17760, posted 15 Sep 2026. K7^= is K7 with two independent edges deleted. The abstract says they prove the first open case of the conjecture for K7^=-minor-free graphs; the proof rests on a density lemma (every 5-connected K7^=-minor-free graph on n ≥ 6 vertices has at most 4n−8 edges).
events.delivers: Restricted class: every K7^=-minor-free graph is 6-colourable. Since K7^= is a subgraph of K7, forbidding K7^= forbids more graphs, so the class is a subclass of the K7-minor-free graphs. This is a special case of the K7 case, not the case itself. (The search snippet called this a 'weaker hypothesis'; the abstract does not say that, and the minor relation puts it in the narrower class.)
events.remains: Every K7-minor-free graph (the K7 case of HC).
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture; restricted-class case of k=7.

ai.note: Read to 100,000 of 149,004 characters of the HTML; no AI statement in the part read.

events.what_happened: Illingworth and Steiner, 'Disproof of the dominating Hadwiger conjecture', arXiv:2609.35361, v1 28 Sep 2026 (only version). The abstract says: 'We provide our own exposition of a disproof of this conjecture found by ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra.' The counterexample is the complement of a pseudorandom triangle-free graph, built by randomly subsampling a block geometric graph based on the Suzuki–Tits ovoid. MathWorld's secondary summary gives the family as graphs on N = 16^m vertices (m odd, large) with α ≤ 2 and no dominating K_⌊(1/2−δ)N⌋-model; I did not confirm those numbers from the arXiv text.
events.delivers: Disproves the dominating variant (χ ≥ t does not force a dominating K_t-model). The dominating variant implies the original, so this does not disprove the original conjecture; it is silent on it.
events.remains: The original conjecture is untouched.
events.directly_checkable: The counterexample family is a graph construction; the authors' exposition is the only check I found. I did not verify the construction myself.
events.direction: Cuts against the dominating variant. It does not contradict the original conjecture, since the dominating variant is strictly stronger.
events.object: Graphs G, for each sufficiently large odd m, on N = 16^m vertices (per MathWorld), each the complement of a pseudorandom triangle-free graph obtained by randomly subsampling a block-geometric graph built from the Suzuki–Tits ovoid. Per MathWorld: α(G) ≤ 2, χ(G) ≥ N/2, no dominating K_⌊(1/2−δ)N⌋-model for a fixed δ > 0. The construction is random, so the existence proof is likely non-constructive; I did not confirm this from the full text.

systems.name: ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors' abstract, found the disproof. The authors say they provide 'our own exposition' of it. Credited as finding the disproof, so load-bearing on the authors' own account.
systems.basis_quote: We provide our own exposition of a disproof of this conjecture found by ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra.

events.what_happened: Norin and Steiner, 'A Proof of the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture', arXiv:2610.05291, v1 4 Oct 2026 (only version). They prove there is an absolute constant C such that every K_t-minor-free graph is Ct-colourable. Abstract: 'The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions by the authors.' Introduction: the proof 'was developed by OpenAI’s ChatGPT model Astra 6, following research directions'; 'The authors suggested several possible approaches, but almost none of their specific proof ideas were retained.' The introduction also says the Lean formalisation 'was produced by OpenAI Codex versions 6 Sol and Astra'. A Lean 4 / Mathlib repository is at github.com/snorin239/LinearHadwiger; its README says it is sorry-free and was produced by Codex, following the authors' guidance (per my fetch summary, not a verbatim quote). Wikipedia (last edited 11 Oct 2026) reports the claim.
events.delivers: Linear Hadwiger: χ(G) ≤ C·h(G) for an absolute constant C, i.e. every K_t-minor-free graph is Ct-colourable. The constant is not stated in the abstract; Wood reports the unoptimised constant is of order 10^100. This is the linear (O(t)) form, a weaker statement than the exact inequality asked for.
events.remains: The exact inequality χ ≤ h (every K_t-minor-free graph is (t−1)-colourable), for every t ≥ 7 (t ≤ 6 already settled by other means per the events above).

checked_by.qualification: Graph theorist; co-author of arXiv:2512.17114 and other Hadwiger-related work
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a follow-up (arXiv:2610.10831) that optimises the constant in this proof and reports a formal check of the optimised theorem. He does not state an independent verification of the original argument's correctness.
Per Wood: 'GPT-6 checked the proof and suggested further optimisations.' This is a check of the optimised version of the argument.

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 with Mathlib v4.32.1 (per the repository README)

events.doubts: Only about a week old. No expert commentary on the argument found in searches. The Lean README says it formalises 'Theorem 2' and refers to 'Theorem 1' in an earlier draft, whereas Wood cites the linear statement as Theorem 1.2 of the arXiv paper. Whether the Lean statement is the arXiv linear theorem is therefore not confirmed. I did not build the repository, so the sorry-free claim is the README's own.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture. It proves a weaker, linear form; it contradicts nothing.

systems.name: GPT-6 Astra
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors: found the proof, 'following the directions by the authors'. The introduction calls the same system 'OpenAI’s ChatGPT model Astra 6' and says the authors asked it to prove 'the very dense case of Linear Hadwiger’s conjecture'; it succeeded 'after only a couple of hours and some encouragement'. The authors say almost none of their own proof ideas were retained. Load-bearing on the authors' account.
systems.basis_quote: The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions by the authors.

events.what_happened: David R. Wood, 'Tweaking the constant in the Linear Hadwiger Theorem', arXiv:2610.10831, v1 7 Oct 2026 (only version). Starts from Norin and Steiner's linear proof and reports an explicit constant C = 19,885,160 (down from the order of 10^100). The abstract's AI sentence is 'This paper uses extensive AI-based optimisation to show that every graph ...'. The introduction says: 'The present paper simply reports the outcomes of an experiment in using AI to optimise the constants.' Lean 4 verification is reported for Theorem 1.3.
events.delivers: An explicit constant for the linear theorem: χ(G) ≤ 19,885,160·h(G) for every graph G (a restricted form of the linear statement, with explicit C). Not the exact inequality.
events.remains: The exact inequality χ ≤ h; the linear result is unchanged in order.

Per Wood: 'GPT-6 checked the proof and suggested further optimisations.'

events.what_happened: Wang and Wu, 'The Spherical Hadwiger Theorem', arXiv:2608.27305, v1 27 Aug 2026; v2 9 Sep 2026; v3 13 Sep 2026. The paper classifies continuous SO(n+1)-invariant valuations on spherical convex sets as combinations of the spherical intrinsic volumes. This is Hadwiger's characterisation theorem on the sphere, a different problem from the coloring conjecture. A search snippet says the paper's AI declaration credits OpenAI Codex with substantial contributions; the abstract page I opened has no such statement, and the full text was not readable.
events.delivers: Different problem: classification of spherical valuations (convex geometry). Says nothing about chromatic number or clique minors.
events.remains: The graph-colouring conjecture, entirely.
events.direction: Different question; no bearing on the coloring conjecture.

ai.note: Search snippet reports a Codex declaration; not seen in the abstract page or readable in the PDF. Unconfirmed.

It concerns Hadwiger's covering conjecture (covering convex bodies by smaller homothets), a different conjecture sharing the name. The HTML appendix says 'The main argument was found in conversation with OpenAI’s GPT-6 Pro' and that Codex was used 'to revise the exposition and check sources'.
events.delivers: Different problem: covering-number bounds for convex bodies. Says nothing about chromatic number or clique minors.
events.remains: The graph-colouring conjecture, entirely.

We prove that a graph G with no (k+1)-clique minor is k-colorable.' The snippet says the proof 'uses a nondeterministic algorithm'. The venue appears to be the Japanese Society for AI's SIG-AM 26th meeting. Date unknown. The SIG-AM URL that the snippet cites returned a different document when I fetched it (the announcement for the 37th meeting, Dec 2026), so I could not open the abstract; this item rests on search snippets. The only text I have comes from search snippets, because the cited URL returned a different document. The claimed proof is said to use a 'nondeterministic algorithm', which is a computing term and not an AI system.

summary: I ran 38 searches and opened the arXiv abstract page (and the HTML version where one rendered) for every in-window item I found, plus the Wikipedia article, MathWorld page, the Lean repository README, and two older preprints. Binary PDFs could not be read, so verbatim quotes come from HTML renderings or abstract pages read through a summarising fetch; a few quotes are cut at the tool's quote-length limit, and I say so where it matters. Status: no source I opened shows the exact conjecture resolved; the Wikipedia article (last edited 11 Oct 2026) still lists the first open case as k=7. The in-window events that bear on the problem are: (1) the linear form, Norin and Steiner, arXiv:2610.05291 (4 Oct 2026), with the abstract's 'The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra' and an introduction naming 'OpenAI’s ChatGPT model Astra 6' and 'ChatGPT 6-Pro' for proofreading and the bibliography, and 'OpenAI Codex versions 6 Sol and Astra' for the Lean formalisation (the formalisation and proofreading are not recorded as load-bearing); (2) Wood's constant C = 19,885,160 for that linear theorem (7 Oct 2026), crediting Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 in the author's own words; (3) Liu and Luo's O(t log log log t) (6 Sep 2026); (4) restricted-class results, each covering a subclass of the K7-minor-free or other graphs: Norin–Totschnig K7∨ (Jul 2025), Costa–Luu–Wood–Yip α=2 inflations (Dec 2025), Dvořák–Norin–Rahman K7^= (Sep 2026), Carter–Yip co-claw/fork classes (May 2026). The K7 case is the first open one, so restricted-class results are partial progress only in that sense. The variant events (dominating, odd, Seymour–Woodall, Illingworth–Wood, Girão et al., Illingworth–Steiner's dominating disproof) are recorded separately with their AI status: the Illingworth–Steiner abstract credits 'ChatGPT 6 Astra Ultra' with finding a disproof of the dominating variant, and Girão et al. credit ChatGPT 5.6 Sol and Codex with filling in proof details of Theorem 2. The dominating and odd variants each imply the original, so disproving either does not decide the original; I checked this direction. Two different problems share the name and carry AI credits: Gorodzha (Hadwiger covering conjecture; 'GPT-6 Pro') and Wang and Wu (spherical valuation theorem; a Codex declaration that I saw only in a search snippet). A Japanese SIG-AM abstract by Ishihara claims a full proof; I could not open it, and I record it as unverified. Places where a call is close: whether the linear result counts as progress on this problem depends on whether a weaker form counts, which is for the judging pass; the AI attribution for Norin–Steiner rests on the authors' own abstract and introduction, with the README and Wood's paper as corroboration, not press coverage. Where landmark cases are concerned, I recorded each one from Wikipedia or an opened abstract, and I did not trace their journal venues.
competing_reading: Strongest case for counting the Norin–Steiner preprint as a major event on this problem: it is the first proof of a linear bound for the family (every K_t-minor-free graph is O(t)-colourable), the authors credit an AI system with finding it, a follow-up gives an explicit constant and a Lean check, and Wikipedia has already recorded the claim. Strongest case against: it proves a weaker statement than the one asked. The problem asks for the exact inequality χ ≤ h; the linear form leaves every k ≥ 7 open in the exact sense, and it changes only the order of the bound, which the earlier Delcourt–Postle and Liu–Luo results had already moved. On the Japanese claim: a reader who accepts it would count the problem settled; I could not open the text and found no review.
what_would_settle_it: For the linear result: refereed publication or an independent expert reading of arXiv:2610.05291, and an independent Lean build of the formal statement checked against the arXiv theorem numbering (the README's 'Theorem 2' vs Wood's 'Theorem 1.2'). For the Japanese claim: the full text of the SIG-AM abstract (the cited URL did not return it), plus any review or response. For the exact status: an expert statement that the k=7 case is or is not resolved, dated after 4 Oct 2026.
